newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ calls in envoys over Japan nuclear shipment.
newsitem.headline: NZ calls in envoys over Japan nuclear shipment.

text.p: Acting New Zealand Foreign Minister Simon Upton said on Wednesday he had expressed New Zealand's concern to envoys from France, Japan and Britain over a ship carrying nuclear waste through the Tasman Sea to Japan.

"I called in the ambassadors of the three countries yesterday to express New Zealand's very considerable concern about the passage of the ship and the fact that they have not been prepared, despite repeated requests, to give any information on its course," Upton told a questioner in parliament.

Environmental group Greenpeace called on the New Zealand government this week to send an Orion aircraft to confirm the location of the ship, the British-registered Pacific Teal, as it passes through the Tasman Sea carrying processed Japanese nuclear waste from France back to Japan.

Upton said that, although the three nations had given no information on the ship's course, it was now well north of New Zealand and he did not consider it worth the expense to send out an air force reconnaissance plane, although one was on standby.
Japan and its partners insist the operation is shrouded in secrecy to avoid the risk of environmental protests or even of terrorists trying to hijack the highly toxic cargo.
Upton said New Zealand had sought assurances that the ship would not enter New Zealand's exclusive economic zone, but had received none.
New Zealand espouses a strong anti-nuclear stance and passsed legislation in the mid-1980s banning nuclear-powered and armed vessels from its ports.
